problem: The text says 'These six words describe the space inside one cylinder', but the bullets name seven terms: bore, stroke, TDC, BDC, swept volume, clearance volume and compression ratio. A student counting them will think a term is missing.
fix: Write 'These terms describe the space inside one cylinder' or 'These six bullets cover the geometry'.

problem: The reason given, 'the gas is squeezed into the clearance volume plus nothing else, but it starts from the whole cylinder volume', is garbled and can be misread as saying the denominator is Vc plus something.
fix: State it plainly: at BDC the charge fills the swept volume plus the clearance volume, so the top of the ratio is (Vs + Vc); at TDC the same charge fills only the clearance volume, so the bottom is Vc. Hence r = (Vs + Vc)/Vc, not Vs/Vc.

problem: 'one steady pressure that would produce the same work in one stroke' is loose. MEP times swept volume gives the net work per cycle, and in a four-stroke engine a cycle spans four strokes, not one.
fix: Say: 'one steady pressure which, acting over the swept volume, would give the same net work per cycle as the real varying gas pressure'.

problem: 'it carries the full torque of every cylinder at once' is misleading; cylinders fire in sequence and the torque builds up along the shaft from the front main journal to the flywheel, it is not applied as one lump.
fix: Say: 'it carries the sum of the torques delivered by all the cylinders, built up stage by stage along its length, and is stiff enough to keep the journals aligned at all speeds'.
